items.title: Parking tickets sent by mail carry extra charge in Mississauga
items.summary: Car owners who get parking tickets by mail in Mississauga must also pay an extra charge on top of the fine. Mississauga city council recently approved a $10 mail-out fee to be paid by offenders who have parking infraction notices sent to their home. The additional charge will cover costs associated with the City of Mississauga’s new way of delivering penalty notices. Mailing some tickets to registered owners of illegally parked cars is among several changes to City of Mississauga parking enforcement rules that took effect Oct. 1. Parking tickets will still be left on vehicle windshields whenever possible. However, where doing so could be dangerous or otherwise difficult for bylaw enforcement officers, the city can now simply record the licence plate and send an infraction notice to the vehicle owner by mail. “Serving a penalty notice by mail requires additional administrative steps to prepare, quality-check, process, print and mail the notice,” Mississauga’s community services commissioner Raj Sheth noted in an earlier report to council that proposed the new charge. Revenue from the fee, which will be charged only when a penalty notice is served by mail, “is expected to offset the costs incurred by the city in administering the mail-out process,” Sheth added. The report concluded that parking tickets “will continue to be affixed directly to vehicles wherever it is safe and reasonably practicable to do so. ” Situations where placing a parking ticket onto a vehicle windshield may not be the best option include when a car is illegally stopped or parked in a school zone “where vehicles frequently depart before a notice can be safely affixed, potentially creating risks for officers, pedestrians and other road users,” Sheth explained in the report.

items.title: House of the week: Renovated bungalow with saltwater pool in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A renovated bungalow in a sought-after Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This renovated bungalow sits on a landscaped lot in coveted Lorne Park. The residence offers over 3,400 square feet of total interior space. The main level unfolds through an open-concept design with hardwood floors, pot lights and large windows in the living, dining and kitchen spaces. The kitchen anchors the home with direct views toward the backyard, a centre island and quartz countertops. The living room features a fireplace and a walkout. The primary bedroom offers a three-piece ensuite bathroom. Two additional bedrooms and a four-piece bathroom complete the main level. The basement features a recreation room, a second fireplace, two bedrooms, a three-piece bathroom, a laundry area and storage. An additional office/den provides a home workspace, games room, study or potential additional bedroom. A heated, saltwater, concrete pool is framed by landscaped grounds and patio space. The renovated cabana is complete with a television and an electronic roll-up door. A heated garage completes the package. Set within Lorne Park, the property offers access to schools, scenic walking trails, parks, recreational amenities, GO Transit, the QEW and Toronto Pearson Airport.

items.title: A little less spooky, a lot safer: protect your home from CO
items.summary: Mississauga firefighters responded to 495 calls involving CO in homes last year. This November 1 to 7, make time to test your alarms and know the warning signs. Emergency and public safety | October 30, 2026 Once the pumpkins retire, give safety the spotlight. November 1 to 7 is Carbon Monoxide Awareness Week and Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services (MFES) is reminding residents to check their protection about a danger that stays out of site. Unlike Halloween’s make-believe scares, carbon monoxide (CO) poses a real risk. In 2025, MFES responded to 495 calls where CO was present in the home, up from 450 the year before. Knowing the risks, having working alarms and acting quickly can help keep you and your household safe. Known as the “silent killer,” CO is a harmful gas people can’t see, taste or smell. It is a poisonous gas produced when fuels such as natural gas, propane, gasoline, oil, and wood do not burn completely. Sources include fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces and vehicles running in attached garages. People and pets can be affected. You cannot see, smell or taste CO, so dangerous levels can build up unnoticed. Exposure can cause serious illness or death, and symptoms can be easy to mistake for something else. Working CO alarms provide an early warning so you can get outside and call for help.

items.title: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga Introduces Guided Biofilm Therapy With Airflow Dental Cleaning in Mississauga
items.summary: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is now offering Guided Biofilm Therapy as an additional professional dental cleaning option for patients in Mississauga. Mississauga, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 29, 2026) - Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga has added Guided Biofilm Therapy to its dental cleaning services, expanding the options available to patients during routine professional cleanings. The addition introduces airflow dental cleaning as part of the practice's preventive care services and gives the dental team another method to consider when planning a cleaning appointment. Professional cleanings are a regular part of dental care, but the approach used during an appointment can vary depending on the patient and the condition of the teeth and gums. By adding Guided Biofilm Therapy, Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is giving patients more choice in how routine cleaning care may be approached while keeping the overall focus on oral health maintenance. Guided Biofilm Therapy uses airflow technology as part of the cleaning process and can be incorporated when appropriate. The service is not intended to replace every traditional cleaning method. Instead, it can be considered alongside other techniques based on what the dental team observes during the appointment. The addition also gives patients an opportunity to understand how their cleaning will be approached before treatment begins. Some patients may want to know why one method is being considered over another, while others may simply prefer to understand the options available to them. Offering GBT dental cleaning in Mississauga gives the practice a clearer way to explain those choices and discuss how Guided Biofilm Therapy may fit into an individual cleaning visit. For Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga, the new service expands its preventive dental care without changing the purpose of regular cleaning appointments.

items.title: Mayor-Elect Tedjo Pledges Aggressive Push for Long-Delayed Milton GO Expansion
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo said expanding GO train service on the Milton line is among his top priorities as he prepares to take office next month. The outlet reports tens of thousands of Mississauga residents and workers, along with thousands more in Milton, have waited years for two-way, all-day service on the line, which serves stations in both municipalities en route to Toronto. Insauga.com says Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed the roughly $1-billion plan in early 2024 and called on the federal government to become a full funding partner. The outlet reports Ottawa committed in 2021 to cover half the project's cost, but a funding agreement has still not been finalized. According to insauga.com, Tedjo pledged at a Tuesday press conference, the morning after his decisive election win, to aggressively pursue the Milton GO expansion once he is sworn in Nov. 16.

items.title: Ontario Asian Night Market Series Brings First Multi-Day Halloween Event to Square One
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the Mississauga Asian Night Market is hosting its first multi-day Halloween event, called sBOOky Village, in Square One's P6 parking lot from Oct. 29 through Nov. 1. The outlet reports organizer Ruifeng (Ricky) Zhen said this marks the series' 14th event this year, calling the pace ambitious even as time has flown by. Insauga.com says the family-friendly festival blends Halloween and harvest themes and builds on the market's debut at Square One in July 2024. The outlet reports the broader Ontario Asian Night Market series held multi-day events this year in Toronto, Mississauga, London, Windsor, Vaughan, Oakville, Oshawa and Niagara Falls. According to insauga.com, Zhen estimated up to 30 per cent of visitors in Windsor and Niagara Falls crossed the border to attend. The outlet reports Zhen described the year as a whirlwind that also included a FIFA World Cup watch party and mid-autumn and lantern festivals.

items.title: Burnhamthorpe-Molly Intersection Repair Pushed Back to Nov. 4 After Complex Fix
items.summary: According to Peel Region, a partially closed intersection in Mississauga's east end will stay that way until Nov. 4 while crews finish repairing a watermain. The region reports the north side of Burnhamthorpe Road East and Molly Avenue, just west of Cawthra Road, was first closed the week of Oct. 19, with reopening originally expected by Oct. 26. Peel Region says the repair proved complex, requiring crews to move other infrastructure to reach the underground pipe, which pushed the completion date back by more than a week. According to insauga.com, residents had begun asking the region earlier this week why the intersection remained closed past the original deadline. The outlet reports a MiWay bus stop, number 1564, has been temporarily relocated while the work continues. Peel Region is reminding drivers and others in the area to proceed carefully and follow construction crews' instructions.

items.title: Shelter's August Success, 53 Animals Placed, Spurs Return of $25 Adoption Fee
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga is bringing back its $25 dog and cat adoption promotion, running Nov. 2 to 14 at Mississauga Animal Services, to help more shelter animals find homes before winter. The outlet reports the discounted fee is a steep cut from the regular $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens, with HST and licensing fees charged separately. Insauga.com says the promotion follows a successful August campaign that the mayor's office credited with 53 positive outcomes, including 18 dogs, 22 cats, seven rabbits, five birds and one python adopted, fostered or transferred to rescue groups. The outlet reports that campaign drew more than 100 calls a day and dozens of visitors, with seven dogs adopted on the first day alone. According to insauga.com, one long-term resident, a 10-year-old husky and Akita mix named Kaito who had been at the shelter since October 2023, found a home during the August event. The outlet reports the city is launching the new round of discounted adoptions as winter approaches, a period when adoptions typically slow.

items.title: Matheson Boulevard Gains One of the GTA's Largest Multicultural Grocery Stores
items.summary: According to a news release distributed via Newswire, Food World Plus opened its doors Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East in Mississauga. The company, backed by JDass Corp, says the 176,000-square-foot store ranks among the largest multicultural grocery destinations in the GTA. The release states the store was built to serve Mississauga's diverse communities, stocking groceries from Europe, the Caribbean, the Middle East, East Asia and South Asia alongside fresh produce, meat, seafood, bakery items and prepared foods. Food World Plus describes the format as combining a large supermarket's convenience with the variety of an international food market, aimed at shoppers who would otherwise need to visit several stores to find ingredients for different cuisines. The announcement frames the opening as adding a major new grocery option to the Matheson Boulevard corridor.

items.title: CBSA Dog Aggie Flags 16 Kilograms of Undeclared Goat Feet and Ghee at Pearson
items.summary: According to the Canada Border Services Agency, detector dog Aggie intercepted another large shipment of undeclared food at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. The agency reports the seizure included 16 kilograms of goat feet, chicken, ghee and milk powder brought in by a group of travellers arriving from Pakistan. CBSA says the travellers were fined $1,350 for failing to declare the items. The agency reports this is the latest in a series of food and animal product seizures publicized at Pearson throughout 2026. According to the CBSA, Canadian law requires travellers to declare all food, plant and animal products entering the country. The agency says undeclared or improperly permitted goods can be confiscated, destroyed or ordered removed from Canada.

items.title: Dorothy McCaull (Dot)
items.summary: Mississauga, Ontario - With sadness in our hearts we share the passing of Dorothy McCaull. Peacefully in her sleep at the age of 96, on Monday, April 13, 2026. Dorothy loving wife of 50 years to Leslie McCaull (deceased 2000). Loving mother to John McCaull (deceased 2009), Judy Grant (Pat, deceased 2022), Vicki Southon (Brad); adoring Nannie to Brandon, Tyler, Clayton Miranda and Matthew; and GG to Damon. Dorothy lived a life of travel and adventure with many stores to share. Whether it was camping, boating and snowmobiling or enjoying family outings. The family would like to thank the staff of Cooksville Care Center, for the wonderful care and support she received in last year's. A private interment will be held at a later date. items.title: Morguard Marks Topping-Off of 431-Unit Rental Project Near Cawthra and Atwater
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Morguard Corporation held a topping-off ceremony this month for its Boulevard on the Green rental development at 725 Village Green Blvd. in Mississauga, with occupancy expected to begin next year. The outlet reports Brian Athey, Morguard's senior vice president of development, said the fully enclosed building marked the milestone with a ceremonial glass plaque guests were invited to sign. Insauga.com says the project, which broke ground in October 2024 near Cawthra Road and Atwater Avenue, will bring 431 new purpose-built rental units to the city across three mid-rise buildings and townhomes. According to the outlet, the property's zoning allowed for towers up to 12 storeys, but Athey said Morguard chose a lower-rise design to fit the surrounding neighbourhood of single-family homes and townhomes. The outlet reports Morguard has owned the roughly 20-year-vacant site, previously believed to have housed a postal sorting facility, for about two decades.
